lessons.md:
A certificate exam rewards covering the official syllabus, not general knowledge. Starting from the study guide stops you revising things that won't come up.

### The essentials

Open the official AI-103 study guide on Microsoft Learn. Copy every skill it lists into a spreadsheet with three columns: the skill, where you've done it (course or project) and a confidence score from 1 to 3.

Anything scored 1 is your revision list. You've already built much of this outside Azure (RAG, evals, agents, safety); the exam asks how Azure's services do the same jobs. Note the domain weightings: spend time in proportion.

### Worked example

Turn the study guide into a tracker: one row per skill, with columns for "confident", "shaky" and "not started", plus the Learn module that covers it. Update it after every session. When most rows say confident, you're close.

### Common mistakes

- Revising from memory of what the exam "probably" covers.
- Using an old study guide. Check the date on the page.

### Try it

Download the current AI-103 study guide from Microsoft Learn and build your tracker.

check.q: Your revision list should come from:
o: Skills in the study guide you scored lowest
check.e: Start from the official skills list.

lessons.md:
Microsoft Learn's paths are written by the same organisation that writes the exam, so they match its wording and scope.

### The essentials

Work through the Learn paths linked from the study guide, in the guide's order. Habits that save time:

- Skim modules on topics you've built; do the knowledge checks to confirm.
- Slow down on Azure-specific pieces: resource setup, identity and keys, quotas, regions and pricing tiers.
- Keep a one-page sheet of service names and what each is for.

Coursera Plus has Microsoft prep courses if you prefer video; the Learn paths alone are enough.

### Worked example

A steady routine: one module per session, then three questions to yourself in your own words ("What is it for?", "When would I pick it?", "What does it cost?"). Slow down on anything about choosing between services and on security and responsible AI, which often carry many marks.

### Common mistakes

- Skimming modules at speed to tick them off.
- Skipping the knowledge checks at the end of each module.

### Try it

Complete one learning path and mark its rows in your tracker.

check.q: Where should you slow down most?
o: Azure-specific setup, identity and service choices

lessons.md:
Exams ask scenario questions that are much easier if you've clicked through the real portal once.

### The essentials

Reading isn't enough for Azure exams; click through the real thing.

- Create a Foundry project, deploy a model, call it from Python.
- Build an agent with a tool in Foundry.
- Create an Azure AI Search index with vector fields, load your project 1 documents and query it.
- Use managed identity or Key Vault instead of pasting keys.

Set a budget alert first and delete resource groups after each lab.

### Worked example

Before any lab: set a budget alert, create a separate resource group named for the lab and note the region. When you finish, delete the resource group. That removes everything inside it.

### Common mistakes

- Running labs in a subscription with no budget alert.
- Leaving resources running between sessions.

### Try it

Do one lab end to end, then delete its resource group and check the cost a day later.

lessons.md:
The free practice assessment shows you the question style and where your gaps are, which is worth more than another week of reading.

### The essentials

Microsoft offers a free official practice assessment for its role-based exams. Take it cold, under time, once you've finished the Learn paths.

Then sort every wrong answer by domain. Wrong because you didn't know the service? Add it to your sheet. Misread the question? Note the trap. The practice mode in this portal covers concepts; the official assessment covers Microsoft's question style.

### Worked example

After the attempt, sort every wrong answer into one of three groups: didn't know the fact, misread the question, or confused two similar services. Each group needs a different fix: learn it, slow down, or make a comparison table.

### Common mistakes

- Retaking the practice test until you memorise the answers.
- Only looking at the overall score.

### Try it

Take the practice assessment once and sort your wrong answers.

lessons.md:
Turning weak areas into strong ones is where the marks are. Short, focused sessions beat long rereads.

### The essentials

Revise only weak domains, then retake. Aim for 80% or more on two separate runs before booking. Use spaced review: the portal's practice mode resurfaces questions you missed. Explain each weak concept out loud in two sentences; if you can't, you don't know it yet.

### Worked example

For each shaky row in your tracker: reread the module, write a three-line summary from memory and answer five questions on it. Retake the practice assessment only when the tracker is mostly green.

### Common mistakes

- Rereading notes passively.
- Booking the exam before you're consistently above the mark.

### Try it

Fix your three weakest rows this week.

o: You score 80% or more on two practice runs

lessons.md:
Small logistics problems on the day cost marks. Planning them removes one source of stress.

### The essentials

Book through Microsoft's exam page: about £106 plus VAT, 120 minutes, pass mark 700 out of 1,000. Online proctored needs a quiet room, a clear desk and ID; a test centre avoids technical risk.

During the exam: flag and move on from slow questions; read every word of case studies; you can usually open Microsoft Learn during role-based exams, but searching costs time, so use it only to confirm. Add the badge to LinkedIn and your CV the day you pass. Renewal is free each year through an online assessment.

### Worked example

If you sit online: test your camera and connection with the exam provider's system check a day early, clear your desk and have ID ready. If you sit at a test centre: plan the route and arrive early. Either way, flag hard questions and come back to them rather than getting stuck.

### Common mistakes

- Skipping the system check for an online exam.
- Spending ten minutes on one question.

### Try it

Book a date when your practice scores have been above the pass mark twice in a row.
